grades.quote: This section describes a simple paged virtual-memory system for SXLEN=64, which supports 39-bit virtual address spaces.
grades.reason: It introduces Sv39 as the RISC-V paged scheme for SXLEN=64 with 39-bit virtual addresses. It gives no VPN or offset field layout and doesn't mention xv6 walk, so it helps only as background.

grades.quote: walk descends the page table tree one level at a time, using each level’s 9 bits of virtual address to index into the relevant page directory page.
grades.reason: It covers the xv6 side of the question. walk mimics the RISC-V paging hardware, descends the tree one level at a time, and uses 9 bits of virtual address per level to index each page directory page. It also mentions the first and second level directories and the final PTE level. It never names Sv39 or its VPN[2]/VPN[1]/VPN[0] fields, so the mapping to Sv39 is only implied.
It describes Sv32 (32-bit, SXLEN=32), not Sv39. It says nothing about xv6 walk or the Sv39 address fields, so it doesn't help with this question.

It covers system call arguments and copyinstr/walkaddr safely accessing user memory. It only mentions that walkaddr calls walk and says nothing about the levels or address bits, so it doesn't relate walk to the Sv39 fields.
